Bench: Pranay Verma

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pranay Verma

On The 7 th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 19 of 2023
 Goutam S/O Santosh (Minor) Through Natural Guardian
 Father Santosh
 Versus
 Aanand And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Chetan Joshi - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Bhashkar Agrawal, learned counsel for the responde
 No.3/insurance company.

For the reasons stated in the application, the same is  notice of this appeal upon respondents 1 and 2 are dispensed wi  of the appellant.
ORDER With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 04.07.2022 passed in Claim Case No.942/2018 by the IIn d Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.4,54,282/- has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6018 2 MA-19-2023 been awarded to him on account of injury suffered by him in the accident in question.
2. As per appellant on 12.12.2017 at 6:30 pm he along with his son was going on a motorcycle.

When they reached Devi Ji Road, near Veer Hanuman Mandir, respondent No.2 drove vehicle bearing registration No.MP-11-AB-5933 which was owned by respondent No.1 and was insured with Goutam S/O Santosh (Minor) Through ... vs Aanand on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168350033/
1 respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against their motorcycle as a result of which they fell down and suffered injuries.
The appellant was taken to the hospital for treatment were he remained under treatment for a period of twenty days.
3. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.10 Lakhs to him by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3/insurance company by filing written statement to the same.
After evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total sum of Rs.4,54,282/- to the appellant by way of compensation.

4. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that his income which has been assessed by the claims tribunal at Rs.6,000/- per month is inordinately low.
It is further submitted that no amount has been awarded for transportation.
A sum of Rs.5,000/- only has been awarded for pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.5,000/- only for attendant and special diet.
The loss of wages have also not been taken into consideration.
It is hence submitted that the amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6018 3 MA-19-2023 compensation deserves to be enhanced appropriately.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurance company has submitted that just and proper amount of compensation has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellant in which no interference is called for in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have considered the submission of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

7. Though the appellant was a minor at the time of the accident and was stated to be a student then also considering the fact that the accident had taken place in the year 2017 his income could not have been assessed at a meager sum of Rs.6,000/- per month.
Even if he had to be taken to be unemployed then also the daily wages which are paid to a daily wager ought to have been considered.
The amount of Rs.6,000/- is extremely low.
In my opinion, his income deserves to be assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month.

The amount for loss of wages would hence also be Rs.28,000/-
since he was unable to do anything for a period of four months.
For attendant expenses the appellant deserves to be awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/- was special diet and Rs.15,000/- for pain and suffering considering the injury suffered by him.
For transportation he deserves to be awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-.

8. The amount which the appellant would be entitled for on account of permanent disablement would hence be Rs.7,000/- + Rs.2,800/- (For 40% future prospects of rise in income) which would be Rs.9,800/- per month i.e. Rs.1,17,600/- annually.
The permanent disability of 15% and the multiplier NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6018 4 MA-19-2023 of 18 applied by claims tribunal is correct.
Thus for permanent disablement the appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.3,17,520/-.
The appellant is entitled for a total sum of Rs.5,50,645/- to him by way of compensation whereas the claims tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs.4,54,282/- only.
Thus the appellant is entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.96,363/-.

2 10.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to be and is partly allowed and the appellant is held entitled for award of enhanced amount of Rs.96,363/- in addition to the amount awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be payable to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
11. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE jyoti Goutam S/O Santosh (Minor) Through ... vs Aanand on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168350033/
